items.title: Report-backed operational evidence with uncertainty
items.statement:
Adopt the laboratory region with its inertial chart and fixed-time reading of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], the electric and magnetic fields of [[def-em-fields]],
the charge parameter, frame charge and current densities and charge integrals
of [[def-em-sources]], and the SI units and constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]]. This definition fixes the framework's report-record
vocabulary; it selects no experiment, records no value, evaluates no indicator
and asserts no measurement.

(a) [Primary source] A *primary source* is a declared bibliographic
identification of a report (author, title, date, publication, and the
identification of the passages actually inspected) together with the declared
limits of the reading: which parts of the report were read, which were not, and
any carrier defects (for instance corrupted optical-character-recognition text
of formulae or tables).

(b) [Comparison quantity and measurand] Let $d\ge1$ be an integer. A
*comparison quantity* of dimension $d$ is a declared map from a declared
condition set to $\mathbb R^d$, with declared units, whose components are
finite expressions in specified framework quantities. These may include the
values of $E,B,\rho,J$ at declared events, the charge parameter $q$, and the
declared charge or current integrals of [[def-em-sources]]; declared field
circulations and surface fluxes on the admitted fixed geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]; and declared finite-time or period averages of
specified derived field quantities, including $u$ and $S$ of
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]. An integral or average is admitted only with its
domain, orientation where needed, integration convention and actual
well-definedness hypotheses declared. For example, a component $Q(t)$
continuous on a declared compact interval $[a,b]$ inside the laboratory time
domain, with $a<b$, has the finite Riemann average
$(b-a)^{-1}\int_a^b Q(t)\,dt$ by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]; a
period average additionally declares the period and interval. Field fluxes
inherit the regularity, compactness, boundary presentation and measure/choice
conventions of their fixed-test supplier. A declared detector-response
integral may be used only when its declared model and integral suppliers
establish a finite real value. An extended nonnegative integral with value
$+\infty$ is not a component of this real-valued comparison map or a recorded
finite rate. No existence or finiteness of an arbitrary field integral,
distributional product or detector response is asserted. A *measurand* is a
comparison quantity together with a declared condition description under which
it is to be read. All quantities carry the SI conventions of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(c) [Apparatus and preparation description] An *apparatus-and-preparation
description* is a declared finite record of the apparatus, the preparation,
the controls and the environment in the report's own terms, with the
identification of the passage of the primary source of (a) from which each
item of the description is taken. The definition asserts only that the
description is declared and finite; it asserts nothing about its correctness
or completeness.

(d) [Recorded data and reported observations] For an integer $d\ge1$, a
*recorded datum* is a vector $z_k\in\mathbb R^{d}$ with declared units
together with a *condition annotation* $a_k$, a declared finite text
identifying the declared run condition of the datum and, when the datum is
taken from a report, its locator in the primary source. A *reported
observation* is a declared finite text recording a qualitative observation of
the report. A *record* is a finite tuple of recorded data and reported
observations together with the declared condition annotations. The record
contains no probability space, random variable, distribution, sampling law,
independence assumption, likelihood or coverage statement.

(e) [Calibration model] A *calibration model* is a tuple $(Z,c,\delta)$ in
which $Z$ is a declared nonempty set of *apparatus-output values*,
$c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$ is a declared *calibration map* and
$\delta\in[0,\infty)$ is a declared *calibration-error bound*: it declares
that for every output $o\in Z$ obtained under the declared conditions, the
value of the comparison quantity of (b) lies in the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[c_j(o)-\delta,\,c_j(o)+\delta]$ in the declared units. A
calibration model is a declaration; the definition asserts no accuracy beyond
the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$. A declared
*missing* calibration is recorded as missing, and no value or bound is then
available from this clause.

(f) [Uncertainty record] An *uncertainty record* is a finite tuple of declared
bounds, each carrying a declared *source label* from the finite list
$\{calibration,\ resolution,\ systematic,\ sampling-variability,\ rounding,\ other\}$
and a declared value in the declared units; each entry is a declared
constraint of the form of (e), and the record may state that a bound is
unavailable. No entry is a standard-deviation convention, a coverage
probability, a confidence level, a $p$-value, a posterior or a probability
law.

(g) [Analysis assumptions] An *analysis-assumption list* is a finite tuple of
declared assumptions used to obtain the recorded data or to compare them with
a model (binning, background model, selection rules, corrections, fitting or
estimation procedure, independence or dependence of entries, and the
treatment of the sources of uncertainty); declared omissions are recorded as
omissions and are not filled in by the definition.

(h) [Interpretation] An *interpretation* is a declared statement that
identifies a specified model prediction and declares the result of comparing
the record with it (support, constraint, failure to distinguish, or no
conclusion), conditional on (a)-(g). The interpretation is part of the report
account and not of the data; it asserts no probability, no significance level
and no truth of any framework, and it records a comparison of a specified
model, not of a whole theory.

(i) [Well-definedness and scope] All components of (a)-(h) are finite tuples,
real numbers, declared maps on declared sets and finite text labels; forming
this finite vocabulary uses no choice principle. Evaluating a comparison
quantity inherits every hypothesis and axiom of its actual suppliers,
including countable choice when the selected fixed-test surface or
Lebesgue-measure interface requires it; no measurability, integrability,
completeness or differentiability is inferred merely from the record. A
comparison quantity is evaluated only where the cited items supply its
ingredients and a finite value. Missing source detail stays missing: no
universal sampling law, precision, independence, coverage or calibration
correctness is part of the definition, and none may be inferred from it. The
definition is the framework-local vocabulary for the reports of this page; it
does not assert that any laboratory realises a measurand or that any reported
observation is correct.
items.strategy: An explicit finite record definition, not a field or apparatus theorem. Clauses (a)-(h) declare finite tuples, real vectors, maps, labels, conditions and interpretations; calibration boxes require only the declared $\delta\ge0$. The enlarged clause (b) names the observables actually used by consumers: fixed-time electric flux on the admitted geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and componentwise finite-time or period averages of the derived quantities of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]. Their evaluation is conditional on the cited contracts. In particular the latter definition makes $u,S$ continuous in the smooth branch, so restricting to a compact time interval gives real continuous components and [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]] supplies finite Riemann integrals. It does not make weak-field products integrable automatically. The fixed-test geometry's compactness, orientation, regularity and countable-choice measure conventions remain explicit prerequisites of a selected flux evaluation. A further detector model must separately supply measurable integrands and finite values before its response can be a real comparison quantity; an extended infinite value is not a finite datum. The syntax of this vocabulary is choice-free, while selected evaluations carry their suppliers' axioms. Missing calibration, sampling or source information stays missing. No measurement, probability law, accuracy or correctness of an apparatus is deduced.

items.physical_scope: Framework-local vocabulary for report-backed operational evidence in classical electromagnetism: comparison quantities built from the fields and sources of the framework at declared events or regions in the SI units of the laboratory frame; apparatus-and-preparation descriptions; finite recorded data or reported qualitative observations with condition annotations; calibration models with a declared error bound; uncertainty records with declared source labels; analysis-assumption lists; and qualified interpretations. The definition asserts no measurement, no apparatus behaviour, no sampling law, no precision, no independence, no coverage, no calibration correctness, no empirical support and no value of any physical constant; it selects no experiment and missing report detail stays missing.

items.title: Faraday's 1831 induction experiments: reported transients and the iron-ring apparatus
items.statement:
**Primary source and reading limits.** Michael Faraday, *Experimental Researches in
Electricity*, Volume I, First Series (read 24 November 1831), 1849 collected
second edition, read in the Project Gutenberg transcription derived from
BnF/Gallica images; the First Series paragraphs 1-33 were read completely, and
no claim is made to have read the whole volume. This is an original report
reprint transmitted by a later transcription, not a newly repeated experiment.
The account below is the report's apparatus descriptions and reported
observations, structured by the record contract of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]; it is not a deduction, and 'no perceived
deflection' is everywhere the report's finite-resolution verbal observation.

## Setup

Insulated copper helices wound on a wooden cylinder, each containing about
twenty-seven feet of wire and kept from touching by interposed twine, twelve
helices superposed in the same direction with the first, third, fifth, seventh,
ninth and eleventh joined into one helix and the remainder into a second
(paragraph 6). A pair of two-hundred-and-three-foot coils interleaved as a
spiral on a wooden block with metallic contact prevented by twine (paragraph
10). A small hollow helix wound on a glass tube into which a steel needle could
be inserted (paragraph 13). Insulated zigzag wire boards moved relatively to
one another (paragraph 18). A welded soft-iron ring, seven-eighths of an inch
thick and six inches in external diameter, with three insulated inducing
helices A of about twenty-four feet each and a separate helix B made from
about sixty feet of wire in two pieces. The A helices were joined end to end
and connected to a battery of ten pairs of plates; B was connected to a
galvanometer three feet from the ring (paragraphs 27-28). Paragraph 31 reports
the ring trial with one hundred pairs; paragraph 11 reports a separate
coil trial with one hundred and twenty pairs.

## Procedure

Making and breaking the battery circuit of the inducing helix while the
detector loop is kept complete (paragraphs 10-11); removing the inserted needle
before breaking the battery contact, and inserting it after make but before
break (paragraphs 13-14);
completing the detector circuit before the battery contact is made or broken
(paragraph 17); moving the zigzag boards together and apart with a steady
battery current (paragraphs 18-19); reversing the direction of the battery
connection (paragraph 30); repeating with larger batteries and with charcoal
contacts (paragraphs 31-32).

## Observations

A slight deflection of the galvanometer needle at the moment of completing the
connection, always in one direction, with the opposite deflection at breaking,
and no sustained perceived deflection under the continued steady battery
connection (paragraphs 11 and 28-31); magnetization of an inserted steel needle,
with opposite poles at make and at break and near-cancellation when both
transients act on the same inserted needle (paragraphs 13-17); opposite
transient deflections as the boards approach and recede, with return to the
ordinary position when the movement ceases (paragraphs 18-20); a minute spark
at the secondary helix with charcoal contacts (paragraph 32); and the control
that, after the first effect, the galvanometer needle resumes its position
under the continued battery current (paragraphs 28 and 33). These are reported
finite-resolution qualitative observations.

## Uncertainty

The read passages identify deflection direction, needle-pole comparison,
battery reversal and background and timing controls, but supply no calibrated
conversion from deflection to current, no detector response or transfer
function, no trial-level dataset, no declared sampling law, no error bars and
no formal significance test; dimensions, wire lengths and battery plate counts
are historical approximate apparatus descriptions, not modern precision
estimates. The sign interpretation of the induced current depends on
galvanometer and needle response conventions. Missing information is retained
as missing; no error bars, precision or independence are invented.

## Interpretation

The reported observations support a transient induction model for the described
apparatus under the stated apparatus assumptions and are qualitatively
consistent with conditional framework predictions of transient induction where
those are instantiated for the described circuits; they do not establish a
universal exact induction law, do not isolate all auxiliary assumptions
(magnetic inertia, switching transients, leakage, current history, geometry)
and supply no quantitative model comparison. The empirical support is a
nonlogical relation to the induction predictions, not a proof of any
postulate, and the source limitations of the reading travel into any downstream
conclusion.
items.strategy: Source-backed experiment exposition, not a deductive proof. Author the five public sections and the recorded observations from the actually read paragraphs 1-33 of the stamped Project Gutenberg transcription (https://www.gutenberg.org/files/14986/14986-h/14986-h.htm, read extent and source limitations preserved in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/classical-electromagnetism/scaffold/faraday-primary-reading.json): apparatus from paragraphs 6, 10, 13, 18 and 27-28; procedure from paragraphs 10-11, 13, 17, 18-19 and 30; reported observations from paragraphs 11, 13-17, 18-20 and 28-33; uncertainty and interpretation from the absence of calibration, sampling and significance detail in those paragraphs. Keep the record structure of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] (source, apparatus/preparation, recorded data or reported observations, calibration model marked missing, uncertainty record, analysis assumptions, interpretation) and set `empirical_result` with the qualitative observation summary, the 'no calibration, dataset or sampling law reported' uncertainty statement, the stated apparatus conditions and the source URL. Do not transcribe a deflection-to-current model, a dataset or an uncertainty interval; the qualitative account remains qualitative. Leave provenance.proof not-applicable, with no Proof section and no proof-audit claim; independent source reviewers check faithfulness, calibration/sampling caveats and the interpretation against the stamped text.

empirical_result.observation: Reported make/break transient galvanometer deflections in opposite directions with no sustained perceived deflection under continued battery current; needle magnetization with opposite poles at make and break; opposite approach/recede deflections returning to the ordinary position when motion ceases; stronger iron-ring transients with battery-direction reversal (paragraphs 11, 13-17, 18-20, 28-33); qualitative finite-resolution observations only.
empirical_result.uncertainty: No calibrated deflection-to-current conversion, detector response function, trial-level dataset, declared sampling law, error bars or significance test in the read paragraphs; apparatus dimensions are historical approximations; 'none perceived' is not an exact zero. No precision is inferred.
empirical_result.conditions: Insulated copper helices and interleaved coil pairs (including the one-hundred-and-twenty-pair battery trial of paragraph 11), hollow helix with steel needle, zigzag wire boards, and a welded soft-iron ring with three inducing A helices and a separate B helix connected to the galvanometer, driven with ten and one hundred pairs of plates (paragraphs 27-31), with make/break, battery-reversal, needle-insertion-order and detector-circuit-timing controls, as described in the First Series.

items.physical_scope: Primary-report account of Faraday's 1831 induction experiments for the described apparatus: transient deflections at make and break of the battery circuit, needle magnetization and reversal controls, relative-motion transients, and the soft-iron-ring apparatus. Qualitative observations with finite resolution; no calibrated current, no sampling law, no precision, no single quantitative model comparison, and no proof or refutation of any induction law or postulate is claimed.

items.title: Hertz's 1888 finite-velocity tests: sparks, wire nodes and qualitative interference
items.statement:
**Primary source and reading limits.** Heinrich Hertz, 'On the finite velocity
of propagation of electromagnetic actions' (Berlin Academy, 2 February 1888;
*Wiedemann's Annalen* 34 p. 661), in the authorized English *Electric Waves*
translation (D. E. Jones, Macmillan 1893), Chapter VII, printed pp. 107-123; the
complete chapter narrative was read in the Internet Archive OCR of
`electricwavesbe00hertgoog`, whose tables are visibly scrambled and have not
been reconstructed or recomputed, and the rest of the volume was not read. This
is a primary-report translation with an OCR limitation, not a modern
replication or a measured-$c$ precision source. The account below is the
report's apparatus descriptions, procedures and reported observation
indicators, structured by the record contract of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]].

## Setup

A spark-excited primary conductor with brass end plates and a central spark gap
drove rapid oscillations; circular or square secondary conductors with
micrometer-adjusted spark gaps served as qualitative detectors; the comparison
used waves on a long wire versus direct action through air, with tuned
secondary orientations and adjustable additional wire length; the room was
darkened, and reflections and nearby fixtures were apparatus concerns (chapter
VII narrative, printed pp. 107-123).

## Procedure

Locating nodal points of the wire standing wave by moving the tuned secondary
along the wire and marking their positions with paper riders; comparing spark
strength and suppression at different positions along a defined baseline;
lengthening the added wire from 100 cm to 600 cm in 50 cm increments and
repeating the comparison (printed pp. 117-118); changing the distance between
the primary and secondary circuits;
and comparing the direct air-path action with the wire-wave action (chapter VII
narrative).

## Observations

Orientation-dependent spark responses of the secondary detector; approximately
recurring and roughly equally spaced nodal points along the wire; and changing
signs of the interference indicator as the path length or the distance is
varied. These are the reported observed indicators; the finite phase delay and
the propagation speed of the order of light speed are the author's
model-dependent inferences, requiring his assumed oscillator, detector,
wire-wave and air-path phase interpretation.

## Uncertainty

The report expressly treats its inferred absolute period from circuit theory as
doubtful beyond order of magnitude; it supplies no modern calibrated
spark-intensity transfer function, no independent absolute period calibration,
no trial-level likelihood or sampling model, no confidence interval and no
synchronized-clock travel-time measurement; the numerical tabular signs cannot
be faithfully recovered from the OCR used, and no quantitative fit, exact speed
or uncertainty interval is claimed here. The author's rough order-of-magnitude
remarks are not confidence intervals.

## Interpretation

The described apparatus observations qualitatively support finite-propagation
and wave-interference models under the stated auxiliary assumptions; they do
not deductively prove the Maxwell equations, do not exactly establish the value
of $c$, and do not eliminate every alternative, since the comparison involves
the assumed oscillator, detector and wire-wave models. The historical
decomposition into separately propagating electrostatic and electromagnetic
components is not promoted to a modern Lorentz-covariant theorem. The source
limitations travel into any downstream historical or empirical conclusion, and
the support is a nonlogical relation to the wave predictions.
items.strategy: Source-backed experiment exposition, not a deductive proof. Author the five public sections from the actually read chapter VII narrative in the stamped Internet Archive OCR (https://archive.org/download/electricwavesbe00hertgoog/electricwavesbe00hertgoog_djvu.txt; read extent, OCR limitation and source limitations preserved in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/classical-electromagnetism/scaffold/hertz-primary-reading.json): apparatus and oscillator/detector description, the node-marking and wire-length comparison procedure, the orientation- and distance-dependent indicator observations, and the explicit separation of reported indicators from the author's model-dependent inferences. Keep the record structure of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] and set `empirical_result` with the qualitative indicator summary, the 'no calibrated transfer function, absolute period calibration, sampling law or confidence interval' uncertainty statement, the stated wire/air comparison conditions and the source URL. Do not reconstruct the scrambled numerical tables, do not invent counts or precision, and do not present the order-of-magnitude speed estimate as a measurement of $c$. Leave provenance.proof not-applicable with no Proof section; independent source reviewers check the reported-observation extent against the stamped text.

The roughly light-speed value is a model-dependent inference, not a synchronized-clock measurement.

Qualitative historical observations with an explicit OCR limitation; no calibrated intensity, period or speed, no sampling law, no confidence interval, no proof of the Maxwell equations and no exact measurement of $c$ is claimed.

items.title: Cavendish's enclosed-globe inverse-square nulls with a sensitivity control
items.statement:
**Primary source and reading limits.** Henry Cavendish's original manuscripts as
edited by J. Clerk Maxwell, *The Electrical Researches of the Honourable Henry
Cavendish* (Cambridge 1879), 'Experimental determination of the law of electric
force', arts. 217-235, printed pp. 104-113, with the detector and electrometer
descriptions arts. 244-249, printed pp. 119-121; read in the Internet Archive
OCR of `electricalresea00cavegoog`. The original apparatus, procedure, reported
observations and sensitivity check are identifiable, but the fractional
calibration ratios and the exponent computation are corrupted by the OCR and no
numerical exponent limit is transcribed or recomputed here. The account below
is the report's descriptions and observations structured by the record contract
of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]; it is a reported finite-resolution
null, not a proof that a true charge is exactly zero.

## Setup

A conducting inner globe 12.1 inches in diameter, supported by a glass stick
coated with sealing wax, enclosed between two tinfoil-coated pasteboard
hemispheres 13.3 inches in diameter with a small clearance, the two hemispheres
applied to each other to form a complete sphere; a removable wire connected the
inner globe and the hemispheres, and could be drawn out by a silk string;
linked strings operated the apparatus so that the charging wire, the inner
connecting wire and the hemispheres were successively separated (paragraphs
219-222). A coated glass jar and an electrometer monitored and repeated the
charging level through a separate electrometer fastened to the prime conductor
(paragraphs 224-225). The inner-globe detector was a pair of pith balls
about one-fifth of an inch in diameter on fine linen threads (paragraphs
220-222 and 244). The paper-cylinder electrometer of paragraph 248 monitored
charging; the later straw electrometer with cork balls, suspended from the
prime conductor, served that monitoring role in the subsequent charge-comparison
experiments (paragraph 249), rather than replacing the inner-globe detector in
the reported null tests. A second experiment enclosed
a wooden piece between two wooden drawers forming a hollow box (paragraph 235).

## Procedure

The hemispheres were charged from a Leyden vial through a wire, which was then
withdrawn; immediately afterwards the wire connecting the inner globe and the
hemispheres was drawn out by the silk string, the hemispheres were separated
without touching the inner globe, and the outer shells and charging wire were
discharged; a pith-ball detector was then brought to the inner globe
(paragraphs 220-222 and 226). For greater sensitivity the pith balls were
precharged positively before the charge, the comparison being made against the
negative-precharge case at monitored equal charging levels (paragraphs
228-229). For the sensitivity control the hemispheres and their frames were
removed, leaving the globe and pith balls. A smaller coated glass element was
charged to the monitored level and its charge transferred to the initially
uncharged main jar; that jar then charged the exposed globe. After withdrawal
of the charging wire the precharged pith balls were compared (paragraph 230).
The report's fractional charge comparisons are unusable in this OCR; no
calibrated charge value is assigned here.

## Observations

Several repetitions without perceived pith-ball separation or signs of residual
inner charge (paragraph 227); in the precharged-ball comparison, equal small
residual separations for positive and negative precharge rather than a
detectable charge-sign asymmetry (paragraphs 228-229); in the sensitivity
control, the small deliberately imposed charge was visibly distinguished by
the same detector (paragraph 230); and a corresponding qualitative null with
the enclosed-box geometry (paragraph 235). The reported 'must be inversely as
the square' inference (paragraph 232) is recorded as the author's conclusion
from the null under his theory, not as a modern theorem.

## Uncertainty

The read passages supply charge-level monitoring, the precharge comparison, a
deliberate sensitivity check and the pith-ball and electrometer construction,
but no calibrated charge transfer function, no trial-level sampling model, no
confidence interval and no modern SI traceability. Insulation leakage, finite
separation time, imperfect spherical geometry, shell holes, accidental contact
and outside charges are apparatus-model and systematic conditions. The OCR
cannot faithfully recover all fractional calibration ratios or the exponent
calculation, so no numerical exponent bound, precision, likelihood or certainty
is invented.

## Interpretation

An ideal inverse-square enclosed-conductor equilibrium model predicts zero
charge in the connected enclosed interior under its idealization, and the
reported observations support that model within the apparatus sensitivity and
auxiliary assumptions; they constrain specified alternative force laws only
after an explicit response and sensitivity model, which the read passages do
not supply in numerically usable form. A finite null cannot prove an exact
exponent, and the empirical support is a nonlogical relation to the static
prediction.
items.strategy: Source-backed experiment exposition, not a deductive proof. Author the five public sections and `empirical_result` from the actually read arts. 217-235 and 244-249 of the stamped Internet Archive OCR (https://archive.org/download/electricalresea00cavegoog/electricalresea00cavegoog_djvu.txt; read extent and OCR limitation preserved in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/classical-electromagnetism/scaffold/cavendish-primary-reading.json): apparatus from arts. 219-222 and 244-249; procedure from arts. 220-226, 228-230; observations from arts. 227-235; uncertainty from the absent calibration ratios and sampling model, retaining the OCR corruption explicitly; interpretation restricted to the qualitative null and the sensitivity control. Keep the record structure of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] and set `empirical_result` with the qualitative null/sensitivity summary, the 'no calibrated transfer function, trial sampling law or numerical exponent bound' uncertainty statement, the stated apparatus conditions and the source URL. Do not transcribe the corrupted fractional ratios, do not invent an exponent limit, and do not promote art. 232's 'must' to an unconditional theorem. Leave provenance.proof not-applicable with no Proof section; independent source reviewers check the null and sensitivity-control reading against the stamped text.

empirical_result.observation: Several repetitions without perceived pith-ball separation or signs of residual inner charge on the enclosed globe (art. 227); equal small residual separations under positive and negative detector precharge rather than a sign asymmetry (arts. 228-229); a deliberately imposed small charge visibly distinguished by the same detector (art. 230); and a qualitative null with an enclosed-box geometry (art. 235).
empirical_result.uncertainty: No calibrated charge transfer function, trial-level sampling model, confidence interval or numerical exponent bound in the read passages; the fractional calibration ratios and exponent computation are corrupted in the OCR and were not transcribed or recomputed; insulation leakage, finite separation time, imperfect geometry, shell holes, accidental contact and outside charges are apparatus-model conditions.
empirical_result.conditions: Conducting inner globe enclosed between two tinfoil-coated pasteboard hemispheres with a removable inner-outer connecting wire and string-operated separation; charging from a Leyden vial with a separate prime-conductor electrometer monitoring the charging level; inner-globe pith-ball detector (about 1/5 inch balls); a second enclosed-box geometry. The later straw electrometer of art. 249 is a prime-conductor charging monitor in the subsequent charge-comparison experiments.

items.physical_scope: Primary-report account of Cavendish's enclosed-globe null tests of the inverse-square law: reported absence of detectable charge in the connected enclosed interior, the precharge sign comparison, a deliberate small-charge sensitivity control and the box-geometry null. items.title: Conditional predictions and qualified experimental comparison
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as inherited from clause (a) of
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]], which is used in clause (a)(i) below with its
piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure conventions; no other choice
principle is used. Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart, the fields
$E,B$ and the source fields $\rho,J$ be those named in
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]], with its constants and units, and let $R$ be a
record of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] of dimension $d=1$ (primary
source, apparatus-and-preparation description, recorded data or reported
observations, calibration model, uncertainty record, analysis-assumption list,
interpretation). Write $I_t$ for the laboratory time interval. Let
$I_\theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open parameter interval,
$\theta_0\in I_\theta$, and $f:I_\theta\to\mathbb R$ a declared comparison map
of class $C^1$ such that $f(\theta_0)=0$ and $f'(\theta)\ge m>0$ for every
$\theta\in I_\theta$. Suppose the record's declared apparatus-and-calibration
dictionary identifies the comparison quantity with the deviation $y=f(\theta)$
of a declared model family from the exact framework reference prediction $y_0$
of clause (a), and declares the recorded deviation $\hat y$ and the bounds
$|\hat y|\le s$ and $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$ with $s,\delta\ge0$.

(a) [Exact framework reference predictions] (i) [Static branch] Assume the
smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell equations with the regularity
hypotheses of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] (fields jointly $C^1$ on
$\Omega\times I_t$ with the additional derivatives appearing in the displayed
equations existing and continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class
$C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$). Let $(V,\nu_V)$ be a volume test geometry
of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] and let $t\in I_t$ be such that
$\rho(\cdot,t)$ vanishes identically on $V$. Then clause (a) of
[[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] gives
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3=0.$$
On the smooth branch every admitted boundary $\partial V$ whose enclosed volume
$V$ is charge-free has vanishing electric flux; charge-freeness of the surface
alone is insufficient, and the exact framework prediction for the
enclosed-flux observable is the value $y_0=0$.

(ii) [Wave branch] Let $(E,B)$ be the plane-wave solution of
[[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] with data $(k,\omega,e)$ there, and let
$\langle S\rangle$ be the period average of its Poynting vector. Then that item
gives the signed identity
$$\langle S\rangle\cdot n=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\,(\hat k\cdot n)$$ for
every unit vector $n$; if the declared dictionary fixes the comparison
quantity as the magnitude $|\langle S\rangle\cdot n|$ of the normal
period-averaged flux (a declared intensity convention), then the exact
framework prediction is
$$y_0=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\,|\hat k\cdot n|.$$ The absolute value is
part of that declared magnitude convention and is not a consequence of the
signed identity.

(b) [Conditional confinement] Under the stated identifications, every
parameter value $\theta\in I_\theta$ compatible with the declared model
family, the apparatus-and-calibration dictionary and the two declared bounds
satisfies
$$|\theta-\theta_0|\le\frac{s+\delta}{m}.$$ Equivalently, a proposed $\theta$
violating this bound is incompatible with the conjunction (specified family,
dictionary, calibration bound, recorded bound); the conclusion is a
deterministic statement about the declared bounds.

(c) [Status and qualifications] The conclusion is conditional on the declared
family, dictionary, calibration and recorded bounds and on the declared
monotonicity margin $m$; it is not a sampling law, a likelihood, a confidence
level, a coverage probability, a $p$-value or a probability that any model or
framework is true, and it asserts no rejection error rate. Agreement of a
record with a specified family, like disagreement with it, concerns the
conjunction of that family with the apparatus, calibration and analysis
assumptions; a discrepancy may lie in the family, the dictionary, the
calibration or the analysis, and neither agreement nor disagreement proves or
deductively falsifies the adopted framework. The three primary reports
recorded on this page supply, in their recorded read extents, no calibrated
response transfer function, no trial-level dataset and no declared sampling
law; accordingly this item asserts no numerical bound and performs no
numerical application for any of them, and their own uncertainty records carry
their source limitations. Empirical support and its constraints are nonlogical
relations, not dependencies, and any consumer of this item inherits $s$,
$\delta$, $m$, the declared family, the record's conditions and the source
limitations.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** instantiate the cited framework predictions, then apply the cited bounded-error analysis to the declared record dictionary. (a)(i): fix $(V,\nu_V)$ and $t$ as in the statement; the smooth branch of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]] applies under its stated regularity hypotheses, and its clause (a) gives the flux identity; the integral of the identically vanishing function $\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $V$ is zero, so the flux is zero. Only the first Maxwell equation and the test-geometry vocabulary of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] are used; no boundary, decay or symmetry hypothesis is added. (a)(ii): read the exact averaged-flux identity from clause (b) of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] at the unit normal $n$; the absolute value records only that an intensity reading is nonnegative. (b): set $J_\theta:=I_\theta-\theta_0=\{r-\theta_0:r\in I_\theta\}$, an open displacement interval containing $0$. Apply [[thm-em-uncertainty-analysis]] with $n=1$, $U=I_\theta$, base point $\theta_0$, unit direction $u=1$, $F=f$ and the supplier's scalar displacement interval $J_\theta$. Its path is $h\mapsto\theta_0+h\in U$ for every $h\in J_\theta$, and $D_1F(\theta_0+h)=f'(\theta_0+h)\ge m$. For a candidate $\theta\in I_\theta$ take $h=\theta-\theta_0\in J_\theta$; the declared deviation is exactly $y=F(\theta_0+h)=f(\theta)$, so the supplier gives $|h|\le(s+\delta)/m$, the stated bound. Laboratory time $I_t$ is independent of this parameter and displacement interval. The record's declared bounds $|\hat y|\le s$ and calibration bound $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$ are the mathematical hypotheses of that theorem; the identification of the record's quantities with the theorem's $y,\hat y,s,\delta$ is part of the declared dictionary and is not deducible from the record structure alone. (c): scope statement recording the conditional status and the absence of any numerically adequate premises in the three reports. No existence, sampling, likelihood or probability claim is made; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only in clause (a)(i) through [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]].

items.title: Classical material, point-source and mechanical regimes and the quantum exclusions
items.statement:
Every cited conditional result retains its stated hypotheses. In particular, the point-source and causal-wave comparisons below assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) through their source suppliers; this qualification supplies no additional field or self-interaction model.

Record the established scope limits of the classical electromagnetic results
assembled in this framework, with no speculative content. Each clause names
what is and is not supplied; the remark asserts no theorem and adds no result.

(a) [Continuum and regularity regime] The fields of the framework are the maps
of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region, with the regularity class
carried by each statement; the solved branches are the smooth and stated weak
branches of the adopted equations, and every conclusion holds only under its
own stated regularity, domain and boundary hypotheses. No discrete, atomic or
finite-resolution structure of matter or charge is assumed, and none is
derived.

(b) [Material-model regime] The material results rest on the declared
constitutive branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] (the elementary
inertial-rest linear nondispersive Ohmic branch and the causal memory branch
with its declared kernel or transfer-function hypotheses); arbitrary
nonlinear, nonlocal, hysteretic, or beyond-branch anisotropic and strongly
dispersive response is not established by this framework, and each declared
branch carries its own regime of validity, including the finite-band
qualification of the constant-coefficient branch.

(c) [Singular sources and self-interaction]
For a nonzero point charge $q\ne0$,
[[pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence]](a)-(b) gives divergence of the
self-field energy as the inner cutoff is removed; for $q=0$ its displayed
truncated energy is identically zero and this divergence does not occur.
[[rem-em-radiation-reaction-limits]] records that products of a singular
self-field with the charge's own distributional current are not defined by
the adopted source model, and that the emitted-power results concern
prescribed sources and determine no back-reaction. No self-force dynamics, runaway
analysis, finite-size regularization or electromagnetic derivation of rest
mass is supplied by this framework.

(d) [External-force and mechanical coupling] Particle motion enters only
through the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] with a
prescribed external field; the framework determines the motion of a specified
test charge in a specified field and supplies no material law, no self-field
dynamics and no derivation of the particle parameters. Any coupling to matter
beyond the declared branches is an additional model assumption.

(e) [Quantum and ontological exclusions] The framework adopts no quantisation
of charge, no spin or magnetic-moment degree of freedom, no measurement
postulates and no photon model. Its interference results, such as the coherent
cross term of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]], are deterministic statements
about classical wave fields; classical electromagnetic waves interfere, so an
interference pattern alone neither establishes a quantum description nor
falsifies classical electromagnetism, and the framework's field predictions
do not single out an ontology of the underlying field or of a particle.

(f) [Empirical status] The empirical content of this page is report-backed and
qualitative: the records of the three primary reports, in their stated read
extents, carry no calibrated response functions, trial-level datasets or
declared sampling laws, so they support and constrain the specified models
only within their declared apparatus, calibration and analysis assumptions;
agreement does not prove the framework and disagreement does not deductively
falsify it. No measurement, precision, probability or confidence level is
invented or inferred by this remark.

(g) [Status] This is a scope remark, not an established theorem; it records the
limits of the results assembled here and asserts no new result, no measurement
and no proof.
items.strategy: A scope remark recording limits, not a proof. Each clause cites the item that carries the result whose scope is delimited: (a) the field definition and the regularity hypotheses of the statements; (b) the material-closure postulate and its declared branches; (c) the radiation-reaction limits remark; (d) the Lorentz-coupling postulate; (e) the deterministic interference theorem together with the framework's absence of quantum postulates; (f) the report accounts of this page. The remark asserts nothing beyond the cited statements: no self-force, no material law beyond the declared branches, no quantum claim, no empirical certainty. The clause (c) content is the recorded scope of [[rem-em-radiation-reaction-limits]] (the supplier's role in this manifest is formulation-prerequisite rather than the design's physical-result label, since a remark is not one of the established-result kinds; the dependency is on its recorded scope content). No choice principle is used. The self-energy use is the stationary Coulomb branch with q!=0 for divergence and zero truncated energy for q=0; producer radiation scope clause (b) remains escalated pending its owner correction.

items.title: A discrepancy can test auxiliaries as well as field assumptions
items.statement:
Let the record vocabulary be that of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]], and
adopt a declared affine response model in which the model prediction for a
recorded comparison quantity is $$y(s,b):=G\,s+b,$$ where $G>0$ is a declared
response coefficient (with declared units [recorded]/[source]), $s\in\mathbb R$
a declared source-strength parameter and $b\in\mathbb R$ a declared background
parameter in the units of the recorded quantity; the model is part of the
record's analysis assumptions. Then:

(i) [Exact ambiguity] For every $\delta\in\mathbb R$,
$$y(s+\delta,\,b-G\delta)=G(s+\delta)+(b-G\delta)=Gs+b=y(s,b),$$ by the field
arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]] makes $\mathbb R$ a
totally ordered field). Hence the two parameter pairs $(s,b)$ and
$(s+\delta,b-G\delta)$ produce the same predicted value at every recorded
coordinate, and every recorded value or declared closed bound interval
compatible with the prediction of one pair is compatible with the prediction
of the other.

(ii) [Nonidentifiability] When $G\ne0$ and $\delta\ne0$ the two pairs are
distinct, yet their model predictions coincide; consequently comparison through
the affine model alone constrains only the combination $Gs+b$.
For an exact recorded equality $y(s,b)=z$ it fixes that combination to $z$;
for a declared bound $|y(s,b)-z|\le r$, $r\ge0$, it only constrains it to
$[z-r,z+r]$. It cannot distinguish the pairs without additional independent
information that distinguishes them. Independently fixing $b$ or $s$ is
sufficient, though other independently declared constraints can also
distinguish the pairs.

(iii) [Explicit instance] With $G=2$, $s=3$, $b=1$ and $\delta=1$ one has
$y(3,1)=2\cdot3+1=7$ and $y(4,-1)=2\cdot4-1=7$, so the pairs $(s,b)=(3,1)$ and
$(4,-1)$ are indistinguishable by the recorded value $7$ alone; the same holds
for every declared bound interval, since the two predictions coincide exactly.

(iv) [Status] This is a deterministic algebraic nonidentifiability statement
about the declared affine response model. It asserts no property of any
apparatus, no historical value, no dataset and no statistical or probabilistic
claim; it records that a discrepancy (or an agreement) can test the auxiliary
background and calibration parameters as well as the field or source
assumptions of a model, so that attributing a recorded outcome to one premise
requires independent information resolving the ambiguity.
items.strategy: Direct substitution and declared assumptions (the recorded research argument X8 of `worked-example-verifications.md`). In (i), expand and rearrange in the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]] supplies the ordered-field, hence field, axioms for $\mathbb R$: distributivity gives $G(s+\delta)=Gs+G\delta$, associativity and commutativity of addition regroup $(Gs+G\delta)+(b-G\delta)$ as $Gs+(G\delta-G\delta)+b$, and $G\delta-G\delta=0$ with $Gs+0+b=Gs+b$). The same identity shows that any condition, bound interval or comparison expression depending only on the predicted value is unchanged, which proves (i) and the distinctness/nonidentifiability claim (ii) for $G\ne0$, $\delta\ne0$. Clause (iii) is the explicit arithmetic instance $2\cdot3+1=7=2\cdot4-1$. Clause (iv) records the scope: no apparatus, historical, dataset or probabilistic claim is made, and the example uses only the record vocabulary and the real field arithmetic. An independent background or source-strength declaration, when available, is an additional hypothesis of any consumer, not a consequence of this example.

items.title: An ideal electric-field zero and a declared detector-bin response
items.statement:
Adopt the two-beam data and conclusions of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]]:
for $v\in\mathbb C^3$ write $|v|^2:=\sum_{j=1}^3v_j\overline{v_j}
=\sum_{j=1}^3|v_j|^2$, using the scalar conjugation and modulus of
[[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this agrees with
the Euclidean squared norm on real vectors. Use
the complex electric amplitude $\alpha(x)=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ and
magnetic amplitude $\beta(x)=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ of its clause (a),
with $\delta(x)=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$, $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and the plane-wave solutions $(E_j,B_j)$ of
[[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]; and its clause (b) averaged energy density
$$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2$$
with the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as
inherited by the Lebesgue-measure and integral items cited in clause (ii),
which are stated under that hypothesis; no other choice principle is used.
Assume dimensionless $a_1=a_2=:a>0$, $e_1=e_2=:e$ with real amplitude vector $e$, and
$k_1\ne k_2$ with $(k_2-k_1)\times e\ne0$; let $x_0$ be a point with
$\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}$.

(i) [Ideal prediction and its vanishing] At such $x_0$ one has
$\alpha(x_0)=ae(1+e^{i\delta(x_0)})=0$
([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]),
hence the electric field of the superposition vanishes at $x_0$ for every $t$
and the electric term of the averaged energy density vanishes there. The full
averaged energy density need not vanish:
$\beta(x_0)=a(b_1-b_2)=a\bigl((k_1-k_2)\times e\bigr)/\omega\ne0$, so
$\langle u\rangle(x_0)=|a(b_1-b_2)|^2/(4\mu_0)>0$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]] for the positive-definite norm). Thus a claim
that 'the ideal intensity vanishes at $x_0$' must name the quantity that
vanishes.

(ii) [Declared bin response and its finite-rate branch] Adopt a declared
detector model with a Lebesgue-measurable bin $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$,
$x_0\in W$ and $\lambda_3(W)>0$, a finite real response coefficient
$\kappa\ge0$, and a declared nonnegative density $b:W\to[0,\infty)$ whose zero
extension $\tilde b$ (equal to $b$ on $W$ and to $0$ off $W$) is Lebesgue
measurable; this measurability of the zero extension is a declared hypothesis
of the detector model. The declared response functional uses numerical values
in fixed declared units:
spatial coordinates are in metres, so $\lambda_3$ carries $\mathrm m^3$;
$\alpha$ carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ as in
[[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]. Fix a declared SI unit $\mathsf U$ of
accumulated response (possibly dimensionless); a response rate means response
per unit time, in $\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Declare $\kappa$ in
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm V^{-2}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $b$ (including
any constant $b_0$) in $\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Thus
$\kappa|\alpha|^2+b$ is a response-rate density in
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $R(W)$ carries
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. This is a declared response model, without an
empirical identification with a detector output. It is defined by the nonnegative
Lebesgue integral
$$R(W):=\int_W\bigl(\kappa|\alpha(x)|^2+b(x)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3\in[0,+\infty].$$
Here the continuous real function $|\alpha|^2$ is Borel measurable by
[[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]] and Lebesgue measurable by
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]; closure under nonnegative scaling
and addition is supplied by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], and
[[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] defines the extended integral. No
boundedness or finite-volume condition on $W$ is imposed. If
$\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$, monotonicity gives
$$R(W)\ge\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$$ even though $|\alpha(x_0)|^2=0$. For a
constant $b=b_0>0$ this lower bound is $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by
[[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]],
[[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]] and
[[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]; it may be
$+\infty$. The *finite predicted rate* branch additionally requires
$R(W)<\infty$, in the response-rate units just declared. A concrete sufficient case is
$0<\lambda_3(W)<\infty$ and constant $0<b_0<\infty$: the bound
$|\alpha|^2\le4a^2|e|^2$ gives
$$0<b_0\lambda_3(W)\le R(W)\le(4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0)\lambda_3(W)<\infty.$$
For $\kappa=0$ the field contribution is the zero function, without forming
$0\cdot(+\infty)$. Identifying a finite predicted response with a recorded
comparison quantity still requires the apparatus, calibration and analysis
declarations of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]. Thus a finite positive
bin prediction is compatible with the ideal pointwise zero, but an extended
infinite response is not a recorded finite rate, and neither response is an
event probability.

(iii) [Record versus prediction; statistical qualification] The data of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] are a finite tuple of real recorded
values or reported observations with declared conditions, calibration and
uncertainty. The predictions of (i)-(ii) are deterministic field quantities or
a declared extended response functional, with a finite real rate only on its
stated finite branch. Here an ideal fringe pattern describes spatial variation
of a specified intensity or response; a single detection and a finite data
tuple are separate records. Whether a finite record displays a specified
visibility or pattern requires a declared criterion, calibration, binning,
background and sampling assumptions, none supplied by the field calculation
alone. No sampling law, probability of failing a visibility criterion,
detection statistics or measured histogram is asserted. This example
discriminates no classical or quantum ontology: classical electromagnetic
waves interfere and the coherence calculation is a deterministic prediction of
the classical model.
items.strategy: Direct substitution and declared assumptions. (i): substitute the stated amplitude data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]]; at $\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi$ the factor $1+e^{i\pi}=0$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]), giving $\alpha(x_0)=0$ and vanishing electric field at $x_0$ for every $t$; the magnetic amplitude is $a(b_1-b_2)$ with $b_1-b_2=((k_1-k_2)\times e)/\omega\ne0$ by the bilinearity of the cross product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and the nondegeneracy of the Euclidean norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so the magnetic term of the averaged density is positive at $x_0$. (ii): $\alpha$ is a smooth plane-wave amplitude, so $|\alpha|^2$ is continuous. The cited continuous-to-Borel and Borel-to-Lebesgue suppliers, under the already stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, supply its measurability. Restrict to measurable $W$; the explicitly measurable $b$ extends by zero, with positive superlevels measurable in the ambient space. The closure supplier makes the nonnegative sum measurable. Monotonicity applies in $[0,+\infty]$ and proves the lower bound without finiteness. A positive constant background integrates to $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by the simple-integral suppliers. In the finite-volume constant-background branch, $\alpha=ae(1+e^{i\delta})$ and the unit modulus of the exponential and subadditivity of its scalar complex modulus ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]) give $|\alpha|\le2a|e|$. Compare the entire integrand with the constant $4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0$ and use the same monotonicity and simple-integral formula for the finite upper bound; this uses no unproved integral additivity and handles $\kappa=0$ as the zero function. Unbounded or infinite-measure bins retain the extended response contract; only a separately verified finite response can enter the real-valued record vocabulary. (iii): the record structure is that of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]], and the vanishing pointwise value is not by itself the bin response; no sampling model, probability, dataset or observation is introduced, and the classical-wave interference character of the prediction is that of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] clause (d). The only choice assumption is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, declared for the Lebesgue-measure and integral interface used in clause (ii); no other choice principle is used.

items.physical_scope: Conditional classical-wave example separating an ideal pointwise electric zero from a declared measurable bin response with background. All measurable bins of positive measure and nonnegative measurable backgrounds remain allowed, with a response in $[0,+\infty]$; a finite-rate interpretation requires a finite response and the declared apparatus/calibration dictionary. The finite-volume constant-positive-background case provides an explicit finite positive response despite the point zero. No data, sampling law, event probability or classical/quantum discrimination is inferred.
